DEPENDS_ON test: remove cepstrum, does cepstral-decorrelation cease to operate? Yes. Cepstral-decorrelation transforms cepstral coefficient vectors to remove statistical dependencies between coefficients. Its entire input is the cepstrum - the quefrency-domain coefficients that the cepstrum transform produces. Without the cepstrum construct, cepstral-decorrelation has no coefficients to transform, no quefrency-domain data structure to operate on. It literally cannot function. Item 1 (type): DEPENDS_ON is correct - the cepstrum is constitutive of the input data structure. Item 2 (direction): correct, dependent procedure points to its foundational data structure. Item 3 (test): note states removal test and result - without cepstrum, no input data, no operation. Item 4 (object level): both are signal processing constructs, not natural phenomena. Item 5 (sense): both endpoints used as their accepted definitions carve them.

[3 test] SERVES test fails (Law 8d): for whose sake? The note says total variability space 'is the core mechanism by which i-vectors encode speaker identity' — but this means i-vector depends on total variability space, not the reverse. The SERVES test asks: does total-variability-space exist for the sake of i-vector? No — it is a mathematical construct (a low-dimensional subspace learned from training data) that i-vector USES. The direction of benefit runs from foundation to dependent, not servant to master. This is DEPENDS_ON from i-vector to total-variability-space, not SERVES in the opposite direction. The note confuses structural dependency with servanthood.

For whose sake, by design: the total variability subspace was introduced to build the i-vector (EXXTRA, Reynolds et al. 2009) — it is the learned subspace the i-vector projects into. The from-def's own procedure stores T 'as the total variability subspace' and its persistence line pins i-vector extraction as the application; the note states the design role ('the core mechanism by which i-vectors encode speaker identity'). Not identity (Law 8c): the subspace (matrix T) is the machine, the i-vector is the point produced in it — distinct objects, one serving the other. Law 8d SERVES holds. Contingent on the provisional endpoint; void+refund if the entry falls.
